READ-ONLY audit (do NOT edit any files) of the CURRENT shared-hosting implementation in /opt/nxeon (Next.js/Prisma). Goal: a precise inventory of what the shared-hosting product ACTUALLY does today — every customer-facing screen AND every backend capability — so a redesign can be planned with zero guesswork about what's real vs missing vs stubbed.

Produce a structured report with these sections:

1. **Customer-facing panel today** — walk every route under `app/dashboard/hosting/**` and the components it renders (`components/customer/*Hosting*`, `HostingDeployWizard.tsx`, any hosting management UI). For each screen: what it shows, what actions it exposes, and whether it's coherent/complete or thin/stubbed. Note the current information architecture (how a customer navigates: account list → account detail → tabs?).

2. **Data model** — the HostingAccount cluster in prisma/schema.prisma: HostingAccount, HostingPlan, HostingNode, HostingDatabase, HostingBackup, HostingCron, HostingSubdomain, HostingAddonDomain, HostingHostnameClaim, HostingTask, and any App/AppInstall models used by hosting. List each model's key fields (esp. per-account limits: maxSites, maxDatabases, diskQuotaMB, mailboxes, phpVersion, etc.) and relations. This defines what "a plan can have multiple websites" means concretely today.

3. **Backend capabilities (what the provisioner/worker can really do)** — read `lib/hosting*.ts` (hosting.ts, hosting-db.ts, hosting-email.ts), `lib/actions-hosting.ts`, `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts`, and the hosting task handlers in the worker. Itemize the REAL capabilities: account provisioning, per-account scoped MySQL databases (DB Studio), SFTP chroot, PHP version switch, one-click WordPress, the one-click app catalog, per-account backups (create/restore), SSL (SNI/certbot), file manager (webroot), cron jobs, email mailboxes (business-email reuse), subdomains, addon domains, migration. For EACH: is it fully implemented, partial, or stubbed? Cite file:line.

4. **Metrics/telemetry available** — what usage/health data exists or could be surfaced per account/site: disk used (diskUsedMB), bandwidth, inodes, serveHttpOk/serveHttpsOk/healthNote, SSL status. Is there any page-speed / load-time / performance data today (probably not)? Note what would need building.

5. **Gates & gaps** — the ENABLE_SHARED_HOSTING flag and provisioner-inert status; anything security-gated; and a candid list of the biggest gaps between today's panel and a modern hPanel-style one-stop-shop (per-site dashboard, WordPress toolkit, staging, performance metrics, plan/site naming, storage-upgrade flow, isolation UX).

Be concrete and cite file paths. This report feeds a redesign proposal — accuracy about what exists matters more than opinion.

# Shared-Hosting Implementation Audit — `/opt/nxeon` (read-only)

## 1. Customer-facing panel today

**Information architecture: account-list → account-detail → 10 tabs.** There is no per-*site* dashboard — the whole panel is scoped to a *hosting account* (one jailed Linux user), and "extra sites" are secondary resources inside it.

**Route `app/dashboard/hosting/page.tsx`** — manage-existing list only. The order/checkout wizard was moved out to `/dashboard/deploy?product=hosting`; this page just calls `listHostingAccounts()` and renders `HostingClient`. Renders `PortalHero` + a "Deploy new site" button.

**`components/customer/HostingClient.tsx`** (105 lines) — compact account cards. Each card shows: primaryDomain, planName, PHP version, storage used/quota, `maxSites` "extra sites", `maxDatabases`, HTTPS badge, status dot. A `FAILED` account shows an inline "Retry setup" button (`retryHostingProvision`). Otherwise the card links to the detail page. Coherent but thin — it's a launcher.

**Route `app/dashboard/hosting/[id]/page.tsx`** — owner-or-admin enforced via `getHostingAccount` (throws → `notFound`). Header shows domain, status, HTTPS/plan/PHP badges, plus a provisioning banner. Renders `HostingTabs`.

**`components/customer/hosting/HostingTabs.tsx`** (415 lines) — the real panel. Tabs: `Overview, Websites, Files, Databases, Domains, Email, Apps, Cron, Backups, Settings`. All tabs except Overview/Settings render a `<NotReady>` placeholder until `status === "ACTIVE"`. Per-tab:
- **Overview** — summary card (status/plan/PHP/website link); a DNS-pointing card that branches on `isFreeSubdomain` (auto-live) vs custom domain (shows A record `pointToA` / optional CNAME); a **`DnsStepper`** driven by *real* serve-verification (`serveHttpOk`/`serveHttpsOk`/`sslActive`) with a "Check now / Go live" button that sets `recheckRequested` and polls ~45s; four **QuotaTiles** (Storage, Inodes, Extra sites, Databases); an SFTP access strip with reveal-password; `AppCredentials`, `GettingStarted` checklist, and a `TaskFeed`. Coherent and genuinely wired to backend telemetry.
- **Websites** (`WebsitesPanel.tsx`) — aggregates primary + subdomains + addon domains into cards (`listWebsites`), shows installed-app label (derived from DONE install tasks), and exposes: open Files (deep-links to Files tab at that docroot), one-click WordPress install per site, **promote addon → primary** (`setPrimaryHostingDomain`), delete. This is the closest thing to a per-site view.
- **Files** (`FileManager.tsx`) — table listing, mkdir, delete, drag-drop upload + download via `/api/hosting/files`. **No in-browser file editor, no rename, no zip/extract, no chmod.** Backed by chroot-jailed `hostingListFiles/Mkdir/DeleteFile`.
- **Databases** (`DatabasesPanel.tsx` + `DbManager.tsx`) — create scoped DB, reveal/reset password, and a **full 91KB proprietary in-browser DB manager** (`DbManager.tsx`) with Overview/Browse/Structure/SQL/Import tabs, row insert/update/delete, export SQL/CSV, add/drop column & index, optimize/analyze. This is the most complete, hPanel-grade surface in the whole product.
- **Domains** (`DomainsTab`) — primary domain card + `SubdomainsPanel` + `AddonDomainsPanel` (create/delete each).
- **Email** (`EmailTab.tsx`) — thin. Only kicks off the complimentary email subscription (`setupHostingEmail`) then **links out to `/dashboard/email`**; it never lists or manages mailboxes itself.
- **Apps** (`AppInstaller.tsx`) — logo-tile grid, WordPress first then catalog; enqueues install task, shows live installing/done state.
- **Cron** (`CronPanel.tsx`) — create/delete cron rows (schedule + command).
- **Backups** (`Backups.tsx`, small) — create backup + list + restore.
- **Settings** — PHP version switcher (`PhpSwitcher`), plan summary + **`PlanUpgrade`** (tier upgrade, up-only, charges wallet delta), and a "Danger zone" that is **text-only — cancellation is handled by support, no self-serve delete**.

**Deploy wizard** (`HostingDeployWizard.tsx`, 773 lines) — order flow living under `/dashboard/deploy`. Steps: `Plan → Domain → [Install] → Add-ons → Review`. Domain step offers a free subdomain (label under `tempSubdomainBase`) or own-domain; Install step picks a one-click app; **Add-ons step sells extra storage** (`extraDiskGB`, priced per-GB/mo via `lib/extra-disk`); Stripe card round-trip persisted through `sessionStorage`.

**Overall:** the panel is coherent and surprisingly complete for DB, Domains, Apps, Files (basic), and Overview telemetry. It is **thin** on Email (delegated out), Files (no editor/rename), Settings (no self-serve cancel, no standalone storage-add), and has **no per-site dashboard, no WordPress management toolkit, no staging, no performance metrics.**

## 2. Data model (`prisma/schema.prisma`)

- **`HostingNode`** (1083) — a physical shared box. `publicIp`, `sshHost/sshPort`, `rootPasswordEnc`, `hostnameFqdn`, capacity (`maxAccounts` 200, `diskTotalGB` 500), `enabled`, `status`, `lastSeenAt`, and hardening fields (`hardenStatus/hardenedAt/hardenLog`). → `accounts[]`.
- **`HostingPlan`** (1111) — product tier. `slug/name/priceCents`, **`diskGB` (10), `maxSites` (1, = addon domains), `maxDatabases` (1), `bandwidthTB` (1, marketing only — see §4), `mailboxes` (1, -1=unlimited)**, marketing flags (`freeMigration/featured/tagline`), **`phpVersions`** (CSV "8.3"), `active/sortOrder`. → `accounts[]`.
- **`HostingAccount`** (1146) — the unit of isolation & billing. `userId`, `hostingNodeId`, `planId`, **`username`** (jailed unix user), **`primaryDomain`**, `status` (PENDING/PROVISIONING/ACTIVE/SUSPENDED/FAILED/DELETING). Per-account limit snapshots frozen at creation: **`diskQuotaMB`** (already includes extra disk), **`extraDiskGB`**, **`maxSites`**, **`maxDatabases`**, **`phpVersion`**. Billing: `termMonths`, `annualDiscountPct`, `expiresAt`. Health/telemetry: `sslActive`, **`diskUsedMB`, `inodesUsed`, `usageAt`, `serveHttpOk`, `serveHttpsOk`, `healthNote`, `healthCheckedAt`, `recheckRequested`**. Secrets: `sftpPasswordEnc`, `dbToolPath` (Adminer drop path), and the proprietary DB-manager creds `dbMgrUser/dbMgrPassEnc/dbMgrReady`. Relations: databases, tasks, backups, subdomains, addonDomains, crons, hostnameClaims. **Note: no `siteName`/label field — accounts are identified only by `primaryDomain`.** No mailbox count on the account (mailboxes live in the separate email-hosting subsystem).
- **`HostingHostnameClaim`** (1271) — single `UNIQUE(hostname)` registry across primary/subdomain/addon (`kind` enum) — the cross-tenant vhost-shadowing guard.
- **`HostingTask`** (1332) — queued node op; `kind` (18-value enum, see §3), `status`, `payload`/`result` JSON (one-time secrets in `result`).
- **`HostingBackup`** (1349) — `path` on node, `sizeBytes`, `createdAt`. Retention 5 (enforced in worker).
- **`HostingDatabase`** (1372) — `name` (username-prefixed), `dbUser`, `passwordEnc`, `status`. `UNIQUE(accountId, name)`.
- **`HostingSubdomain`** (1401) — `label`, `fqdn` (unique), `docroot`, `sslActive`, `status`. Counts against `maxSites`.
- **`HostingAddonDomain`** (1418) — `domain` (unique), `docroot`, `sslActive`, `status`. Counts against `maxSites`.
- **`HostingCron`** (1433) — `schedule`, `command`, `status`.

**"A plan can have multiple websites" concretely = 1 primary domain (always) + up to `maxSites` extra sites, where an extra site is a `HostingSubdomain` OR a `HostingAddonDomain` (they share the budget). Each gets its own docroot + vhost but they all share one unix user / FPM pool / disk quota / PHP version.**

**App/AppInstall caveat:** the `AppInstall` model (2311) and the `App` model (1475) are **NOT used by shared hosting** — `AppInstall` is keyed to `serverId` (VPS), and `App` is the internal kanban product. Hosting app installs are tracked purely as `HostingTask` rows (`WORDPRESS_INSTALL`/`APP_INSTALL`) whose `result` JSON holds the app label/URL; `WebsitesPanel` reverse-engineers "installed app" from those DONE tasks. The app catalog is a **code constant** `APP_RECIPES` in `worker/hosting.ts:1184`, not a DB table.

## 3. Backend capabilities (provisioner/worker — `worker/hosting.ts`, 1756 lines)

The worker SSHes to the node as root (`connectNode`) and runs shell steps. **Everything real is gated by `ENABLED = process.env.ENABLE_SHARED_HOSTING === "1"`** (`hosting.ts:75`). In `SANDBOX` mode it *simulates* (flips DB rows, fake results); with neither flag it's inert. Capabilities:

| Capability | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Account provisioning** | **Full** | `provisionHostingAccount` (439) → `applyIsolation` (291): creates jailed nologin user, 711 home / 2750 setgid webroot, disk **+ inode** quota (`setquota`), **per-user PHP-FPM pool**, self-signed fallback cert, name-based vhost (443 from second one), branded parking page, and **chrooted SFTP via guarded `sshd -t`** (381-389). |
| **Per-account scoped MySQL** | **Full** | `provisionHostingDatabase` (395) + `buildScopedGrantSql` — grant scoped to one DB only. |
| **In-portal DB manager (DB Studio)** | **Full** | `taskEnsureDbMgr` (1535) creates `<user>_mgr` scoped to `<username>\_%`.*; 22 server actions in `lib/actions-hosting-db.ts` run over an SSH-tunnelled mysql2 session (browse/SQL/import/export/structure/index). **NOTE: this is the subsystem the security memo flagged as a CRITICAL RCE — do not treat as safe-to-ship.** |
| **Adminer drop-in** | **Full** (legacy/parallel) | `taskInstallDbTool` (1500) writes Adminer into webroot at `/nxtools-<token>/`. |
| **SFTP chroot** | **Full** | in `applyIsolation` (373-389). |
| **PHP version switch** | **Full** | `taskPhpSwitch` (1034) rewrites FPM pool. |
| **One-click WordPress** | **Full, automated** | `taskWordpressInstall` (1145): wp-cli download → scoped DB → `core install`, into primary OR a subdomain/addon docroot (`resolveInstallTarget`). Returns one-time admin creds. |
| **One-click app catalog** | **Partial (download-then-manual)** | `APP_RECIPES` (1184): 9 apps (Joomla, Drupal, phpBB, Matomo, Grav, Nextcloud, MediaWiki, PrestaShop, Moodle). `taskAppInstall` (1200) only downloads+extracts + creates a DB; **customer finishes the web installer manually.** URLs are pinned to specific versions (will bit-rot). |
| **Per-account backups** | **Full** | `taskBackup` (1254) home tar + root-owned DB dumps, retention 5; `taskRestore` (1287) destructive restore, tenant-namespace-only DB replay. |
| **SSL (SNI/certbot)** | **Full** | `hostingSslSweep` (614): per-domain HTTP-01 webroot certs for primary/addon; subdomains folded as SANs via `--expand`; **wildcard `*.<base>` via DNS-01/Cloudflare** for free subdomains (`ensureWildcardCert` 509, opt-in `HOSTING_WILDCARD_SSL`). Self-heal in `hostingHealthSweep` (978) reinstalls a stale real-cert vhost. |
| **File manager** | **Partial** | list/mkdir/delete/upload/download only (`lib/hosting-fs.ts`, `lib/actions-hosting.ts:1161+`). No edit/rename/chmod/zip. |
| **Cron** | **Full** | `taskCreateCron`/`taskDeleteCron` rewrite the jailed user's crontab. |
| **Subdomains / addon domains** | **Full** | `taskCreateSubdomain` (1371) etc. — own docroot + vhost, hostname-claim in same tx. |
| **Set primary domain (promote addon)** | **Full** | `taskSetPrimaryDomain` (1589) regenerates vhost, keeps old name as alias, runs `wp search-replace` if WP detected. |
| **Plan upgrade / apply limits** | **Full** | `taskApplyPlanLimits` (1556) raises quota + rewrites FPM pool (up-only). |
| **Suspend / Unsuspend / Terminate** | **Full** | `taskSuspend/Unsuspend/Terminate` (1061-1096); terminate deletes user+home+DBs then deletes the account row (1688). Admin-only (no self-serve). |
| **Email mailboxes** | **Full but separate subsystem** | Not in `worker/hosting.ts`. `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts` (1110 lines) + Mailcow: `addMailbox`, `removeMailbox`, `resetMailboxPassword`, DNS records/verify, deliverability check. Hosting only bootstraps the free subscription and hands off to `/dashboard/email`. |
| **Migration ("we move your site free")** | **Marketing flag only — not implemented** | `HostingPlan.freeMigration` is displayed; there is **no migration task kind, importer, or worker code** for shared hosting. |
| **Usage/health telemetry** | **Full** | `hostingUsageSweep` (790, du+find → diskUsedMB/inodesUsed), `hostingHealthSweep` (920, curl 80/443 → serve flags + note + self-heal). |

Task dispatch: `processHostingTask` (1643) for real mode; `hostingTaskSweep` (1701) has a **full sandbox simulation branch** (1702-1751) that mutates DB rows so the dev panel behaves without a node.

## 4. Metrics / telemetry available

**Exists and surfaced today (per account):**
- `diskUsedMB` / `diskQuotaMB` — real, from `du`; shown as a Storage QuotaTile with a bar.
- `inodesUsed` — real, from `find`; shown as a tile.
- Extra-sites count (subs+addons) vs `maxSites`, DB count vs `maxDatabases` — computed live in Overview.
- `serveHttpOk` / `serveHttpsOk` / `sslActive` / `healthNote` / `healthCheckedAt` — real serve-verification, powering the DNS→HTTPS stepper.

**Exists in schema but NOT metered/enforced:**
- **`bandwidthTB`** — plan spec shown on marketing/wizard cards only. **No traffic accounting anywhere** in the worker (grep confirms zero bandwidth measurement). Purely a number on a card.

**Does not exist (would need building):**
- **No page-speed / load-time / TTFB / Lighthouse / uptime-history data of any kind** — confirmed by grep across `components/customer`, `lib/actions-hosting.ts`, `worker/hosting.ts`. The only "response" signal is the binary curl serve-check.
- No per-site (subdomain/addon) usage breakdown — usage is account-level only.
- No historical/time-series charts (unlike VPS, which has `ServerDiskSample`). Hosting stores only the latest `diskUsedMB`/`usageAt` snapshot, no history table.

## 5. Gates & gaps

**Gates:**
- **`ENABLE_SHARED_HOSTING=1`** — the master switch. Every real node operation (provision, DB, tasks, SSL, usage, health) no-ops without it (`hosting.ts:75`, `worker/index.ts:1502+`). Comment at `hosting.ts:12` explicitly says "Do NOT flip that flag" until security review + staging validation. **Provisioner is inert in prod today.**
- **`SANDBOX`** — dev simulation path (accounts auto-ACTIVE, fake tasks/backups).
- **`HOSTING_WILDCARD_SSL`** + `CLOUDFLARE_DNS_API_TOKEN` — separate opt-in for wildcard certs.
- Node hardening (`hostingNodeHardenSweep`) is deliberately **not** gated on `ENABLE_SHARED_HOSTING` (prep work).
- **Security-gated:** per the security-audit memory, the DB Studio (`lib/actions-hosting-db.ts` + `DbManager.tsx`) had a **CRITICAL RCE**; onboarding a 2nd hosting customer is blocked until that promote lands. Treat the whole `dbmgr*` surface as the highest-risk area.

**Biggest gaps vs a modern hPanel one-stop-shop:**
1. **No per-site dashboard.** The mental model is "account → tabs," not "site → its own home." `WebsitesPanel` lists sites but each site has no dedicated dashboard (its own metrics, WP toolkit, files, SSL, staging). A redesign's core IA change.
2. **No WordPress toolkit.** WP can be *installed* but not *managed* — no plugin/theme/update view, no admin auto-login, no WP-specific security/caching, no clone. `taskSetPrimaryDomain` does `wp search-replace`, proving wp-cli is available to build on.
3. **No staging / clone environments.** No task kind, no cloned docroot+DB concept.
4. **No performance metrics** (see §4) — no load-time, no uptime history, no bandwidth graph. Everything is a single latest snapshot.
5. **No plan/site naming.** Accounts have no friendly label — identified only by `primaryDomain`. Cards get visually indistinguishable at scale.
6. **Storage-upgrade flow is order-time only.** `extraDiskGB` is sold in the deploy wizard's Add-ons step, but `PlanUpgrade` on an existing account is **tier-only, up-only** — there's no standalone "add 10 GB" control on a live account (the `taskApplyPlanLimits`/`extraDiskGB` plumbing exists to support one, but the UI doesn't).
7. **Isolation UX is invisible.** Real isolation (jailed user, FPM pool, scoped grants, chroot) is strong but never surfaced/explained to the customer.
8. **Thin file manager** — no editor, rename, chmod, archive/extract.
9. **Email is bolted-on** — a separate subsystem the hosting panel only links to, not an integrated mailbox manager.
10. **Migration is vaporware** — advertised (`freeMigration`), zero implementation.
11. **No self-serve cancellation** — Settings "Danger zone" is text; termination is admin-only.

**Key files for the redesign:** UI — `components/customer/hosting/HostingTabs.tsx`, `WebsitesPanel.tsx`, `DbManager.tsx`, `FileManager.tsx`, `HostingClient.tsx`, `HostingDeployWizard.tsx`. Server actions — `lib/actions-hosting.ts` (1881 lines), `lib/actions-hosting-db.ts`, `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts`. Worker — `worker/hosting.ts` (all capabilities + `APP_RECIPES` catalog), dispatch in `worker/index.ts:1502+`. Schema — `prisma/schema.prisma:1083-1443`.
